newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan exchanges mull steps to revive sugar trade.
newsitem.headline: Japan exchanges mull steps to revive sugar trade.

text.p: Two Japanese commodity futures exchanges said on Thursday they are mulling ways to attract private investor interest in their raw sugar futures contracts and revitalise trade that has seen a decline in recent years.

The Tokyo Grain Exchange (TGE) and the Kansai Commodities Exchange, the two exchanges that list raw sugar in Japan, said they were thinking of reducing the number of contract months in their sugar futures trade in a bid to boost liquidity.
"By reducing the number of raw sugar future contract months to six months from the current nine months, we hope to revive trading in raw sugar futures," a TGE official said.
"We hope to move into the new system, maybe by July this year at earliest," he said.
Open interest of raw sugar futures on the TGE fell to 71,142 lots as of April 30, down sharply from the record high of 573,840 lots marked on March 21, 1990.
An official with the Kansai Commodities Exchange said a reduction in the number of listed contract months would lift liquidity, making it easier for private investors to participate in the market.
The Kansai Commodities Exchange is also thinking of cutting the number of listed contract months to six from nine, the official said.
Sugar traders said the popularity of sugar futures has waned in recent years mainly because of stagnant prices due to a lack of market-moving factors, and also a lack of liquidity.
Most soft and grain futures contracts in Japan list six contract months.
